recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. Future ImagingStudy source changes should preserve uppercase formal modal terms or deliberately reword non-conformance possibilities to avoid reintroducing lowercase modal keywords.
issue_request: FHIR-47624 was an Applied/Persuasive Imaging Integration technical correction for the R6 ImagingStudy ballot. It requested consistent capitalization of MAY, SHALL, SHOULD, MUST, and similar formal modal terms in the ImagingStudy material, specifically noting section 10.5.2 and generated Requirements text.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by 07c006edb2, which capitalized MAY, SHOULD, and SHALL across ImagingStudy introduction, notes, and StructureDefinition source. Commit 1ac0ca73d6 then made a related QA correction to the ImagingStudy.identifier requirements parenthesis. Those commits addressed the original examples, but later edits left residual/reintroduced lowercase formal modal wording.
additional_context: The ImagingStudy resource is active in source/fhir.ini. Later FHIR-47634 work in d75e2e196f4 changed the ImagingStudy.status comment from SHALL apply back to lowercase must apply, and 578d35b1a7 aligned the mapping exception with that lowercase wording. Later R6 ImagingStudy narrative also introduced lowercase must not and may in active introduction and notes text. The remaining lowercase should in the ImagingStudy status CodeSystem mirrors other status CodeSystems and was treated as shared descriptive code-definition prose, not part of this resource modal capitalization fix.
reconciliation: Published a non-empty source commit on the combined branch. The commit changes the ImagingStudy introduction ballot note to MUST NOT, the endpoint note to MAY require per-series endpoints, the ImagingStudy.status comment to SHALL apply, and the Event mapping exception resource text/reason to stay synchronized with the StructureDefinition.
